subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A stretched rubber band is holding energy in which store?
questions.explain: Stretching or compressing an object stores energy in its elastic potential store.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of energy?
questions.explain: Energy is measured in joules (J); the watt is the unit of power.

questions.q: Which formula gives the kinetic energy of a moving object?
questions.explain: Kinetic energy equals one half of mass multiplied by speed squared (½mv²).

questions.q: A car speeds up along a flat road. Which store of energy is mainly increasing?
questions.explain: Increasing speed on level ground increases the object's kinetic energy store.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the four ways energy can be transferred?
questions.explain: Energy is transferred mechanically, electrically, by heating, or by radiation (e.g. light and sound).

questions.q: A 1000 kg car travels at 20 m/s. What is its kinetic energy?
A 2 kg book is lifted 5 m onto a shelf (g = 10 N/kg). How much gravitational potential energy does it gain?
questions.explain: GPE gained = m g h = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100 J.

questions.q: As a swinging pendulum rises to the top of its swing, energy is transferred mainly from its:
options: Kinetic store to its gravitational potential store
Gravitational potential store to its kinetic store
Chemical store to its thermal store
Elastic store to its kinetic store
questions.explain: Rising slows the pendulum, so kinetic energy is transferred to the gravitational potential store.

questions.q: Which statement is the principle of conservation of energy?
options: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transferred or stored
Energy is always lost when it is used
Energy can be created if a machine is efficient
questions.explain: Conservation of energy states the total energy of a closed system stays constant; it is only transferred between stores.

questions.q: When energy is dissipated, it is best described as being:
options: Spread out to the surroundings and less useful
questions.explain: Dissipated energy spreads to the surroundings (often by heating) and becomes less useful, though it is not destroyed.

questions.q: How is the efficiency of a device calculated?
options: Useful energy output ÷ total energy input
Total energy input ÷ useful energy output
Useful energy output × total energy input
Total energy input − useful energy output
questions.explain: Efficiency = useful energy (or power) output divided by total energy (or power) input.

questions.q: A motor is supplied with 500 J of electrical energy and does 400 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
Why can no real machine be 100% efficient?
options: Some energy is always dissipated to the surroundings, usually by heating
Energy is destroyed during the transfer
All the input energy becomes useful output
questions.explain: Wasted energy is always dissipated (commonly as heat due to friction), so useful output is always less than total input.

questions.q: What is the unit of power?
questions.explain: Power is the rate of energy transfer, measured in watts, where 1 W = 1 J/s.

questions.q: A lamp transfers 600 J of energy in 30 s. What is its power?
questions.explain: Power = energy ÷ time = 600 ÷ 30 = 20 W.

questions.q: Which action would reduce the energy dissipated by friction in a machine?
options: Reducing the oil on the bearings
questions.explain: Lubrication lowers friction between moving parts, reducing the energy wasted as heat.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy resource?
questions.explain: Wind is renewable because it is replenished naturally and will not run out on a human timescale.

questions.q: Which group lists only fossil fuels?
questions.explain: The three fossil fuels are coal, oil (petroleum) and natural gas, all non-renewable.

questions.q: What does it mean to call a resource such as coal 'non-renewable'?
options: It is being used up faster than it is replaced and will eventually run out
It can be replaced within a few years
It provides an unlimited supply of energy
questions.explain: Non-renewable resources form over millions of years, so they are used far faster than they are replenished.

questions.q: Which is a disadvantage of using wind power to generate electricity?
options: It is unreliable because it depends on the weather
It releases large amounts of carbon dioxide
questions.explain: Wind turbines only generate when the wind blows, making the supply intermittent and hard to control.
